scope: XMemMakeTag encoding and fail-closed XMemVirtualQuery placeholder. Query success, Xbox page flags, allocation tags, partition identities and GPU access are unsupported.
abi_evidence: Supplied xmem.dll XMemVirtualQuery export ordinal 32 RVA 0x25d0 accepts process handle, address, and output in RCX/RDX/R8. Static inspection shows 64-byte output with a 48-byte desktop memory-information prefix and console metadata at offsets 48 and 56. XMemMakeTag ordinal 20 RVA 0x7ab0 takes a 32-bit tag and returns a 64-bit value. Additional inspected branches add partition/access flags at offset 48 and allocation tags at offset 56, and can alter State and RegionSize; the packaged DLL could not be initialized for success-path comparison.
query_checks: Reserved, committed and released CPU addresses return ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED with the entire output and guards untouched. A null output returns ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER. Name and ordinal 32 resolve to the same function.

tag_control.native: tools/check_xmem_tag_native.py runs the isolated, hash-checked, call-free reference routine from the user-supplied DLL on x86-64; console bytes are not stored.
tag_control.inputs: All 256 byte values independently in each of four positions plus 4,096 seeded inputs, and zero.
tag_control.match: The Proton guest uses the identical ordered cases and matches the native reference fingerprint. Name/ordinal identity is checked.

checks.receipt: xmem-default: PASS (allocator pairs 1/6 and 2/7, ordinary and 64 KiB allocations, host working set v2, virtual reserve/commit)
